title: Multi-Tenant B2B SaaS Backend with Row-Level Security & Outbox Messaging
problem: Modern enterprise B2B SaaS platforms must enforce strict data isolation between rival corporate tenants, support asynchronous inter-service communication without data loss, and deliver outbound customer webhooks reliably. Naive application-level WHERE tenant_id filtering risks catastrophic data leakage if a single developer forgets a clause, and direct HTTP calls between microservices introduce cascading downtime. This project constructs an enterprise multi-tenant backend in TypeScript and Node.js using PostgreSQL Row-Level Security (RLS) to enforce database-level tenant isolation, Kafka event streaming with the Transactional Outbox pattern to guarantee at-least-once message delivery, Redis for tenant rate quotas, and an idempotent webhook delivery worker with exponential backoff retries.
use_cases: Enterprise B2B SaaS products requiring strict compliance-certified tenant data boundaries
Usage-metered cloud platforms aggregating customer API consumption for billing pipelines
Developer webhook delivery backends guaranteeing reliable event delivery to external customer systems
hard_parts: Enforcing PostgreSQL Row-Level Security policies dynamically bound to active connection tenant session variables
Implementing the Transactional Outbox pattern to atomically commit database changes and publish Kafka events without distributed transactions
Preventing cross-tenant noisy-neighbor starvation through fair-share Redis rate limiting and concurrency throttling
Managing reliable webhook dispatching with HMAC signature verification, exponential backoff, and dead-letter queue routing
screener_signals: Clean TypeScript codebase cleanly separating tenant middleware, outbox workers, Kafka consumers, and webhook dispatchers
Automated cross-tenant penetration test asserting zero cross-tenant row leakage across 1,000 concurrent database queries
Anti-fake verification script creating dynamic tenant accounts, dispatching outbox messages, and asserting strict boundary isolation

components.name: PostgreSQL Multi-Tenant RLS Store
components.purpose: Enforces tenant data boundaries via database-level Row-Level Security policies and session variables

components.name: Transactional Outbox Publisher
components.purpose: Atomically polls outbox table rows within database transactions and publishes domain events to Kafka topics

components.name: Tenant Context & Ingress Middleware
components.purpose: Validates tenant JWT claims, sets database session variables, and enforces per-tenant Redis rate quotas

components.name: Metered Usage Aggregator
components.purpose: Consumes domain events from Kafka and aggregates customer resource consumption into billing ledgers

components.name: Reliable Webhook Dispatcher
components.purpose: Signs and dispatches customer webhooks with HMAC-SHA256, handling retries and routing failures to DLQ

architecture.data_flow: Incoming client HTTP requests pass through Tenant Ingress Middleware; tenant ID is validated and injected into PostgreSQL session config via SET LOCAL app.current_tenant_id; CRUD queries execute with RLS automatically restricting rows to active tenant; mutations atomically insert domain events into an outbox table within the same transaction; the Transactional Outbox Publisher polls pending outbox entries and publishes them to Kafka; the Metered Usage Aggregator consumes Kafka events to calculate usage; the Webhook Dispatcher signs and posts payloads to customer endpoints with exponential backoff.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: PostgreSQL Row-Level Security policies rejecting queries lacking valid tenant context; Redis token buckets throttling noisy-neighbor tenant spikes.

worksheet.q1: Core deliverable: a multi-tenant B2B SaaS backend in TypeScript/Node.js with PostgreSQL RLS, transactional outbox to Kafka, and reliable webhooks.
worksheet.q2: Target users: SaaS backend engineers, platform architects, and cloud infrastructure developers.
worksheet.q3: 3 use cases: enterprise B2B SaaS data isolation, metered cloud usage billing, and customer webhook delivery backends.
worksheet.q4: Stated hours: 39 hours. Calculated bottom-up: 34 component hours * 1.15 buffer = 39.1 -> 39 hours. Advanced level.
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: dynamic PostgreSQL RLS session configuration, transactional outbox atomicity, fair-share rate limiting, and reliable webhook backoff.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: 50 tenant profiles, 25,000 customer records, and 5,000 simulated events. Synthetic profiles only.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 8GB RAM, CPU only, $0 cost, zero cloud accounts. Fallback: SQLite and in-memory event bus.
worksheet.q8: Riskiest component: Connection pool exhaustion from unset RLS session variables. Fallback: automated connection checkout/reset hooks.
worksheet.q9: Potential faking: hardcoded tenant query filtering. Anti-fake check 5 provisions two dynamic tenants at runtime and asserts boundary rejection.
worksheet.q10: Safety/ethics: Safe; synthetic business profiles and mock customer accounts only.
